questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A uniform rod AD of length 4 m is suspended horizontally by two vertical strings attached at A and D, the ends of the rod. The rod weighs 100 N and a weight of 100 N is also attached on the rod 1 m from A.

Given that the system is at equilibrium,

(a) draw a diagram showing all the forces acting on the rod. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Draw the rod AD horizontally, $4$ m long, with A on the left and D on the right. Four vertical forces act on it:

| Force | Where it acts | Direction | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tension $T_A$ in the string at A | at A | upwards | unknown |
| Tension $T_D$ in the string at D | at D (4 m from A) | upwards | unknown |
| Weight of the rod | at its centre, 2 m from A | downwards | $100$ N |
| Attached weight | 1 m from A | downwards | $100$ N |

Mark the distances $1$ m (A to the attached weight), $1$ m (from there to the centre of the rod) and $2$ m (from the centre to D) along the rod. Arrows up at A and D, arrows down at the $1$ m and $2$ m points.
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Hence or otherwise,

(b) find the tensions in the strings. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $T_A$ and $T_D$ be the tensions at A and D.

**Moments about A** (anticlockwise positive, equilibrium):

$$4\,T_D=100\times1+100\times2=300\ \Longrightarrow\ T_D=75.$$

**Resolving vertically:**

$$T_A+T_D=100+100=200\ \Longrightarrow\ T_A=200-75=125.$$

Check by taking moments about D: $4\,T_A=100\times3+100\times2=500$, so $T_A=125$.

**The tension at A is $125$ N and the tension at D is $75$ N.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A crane lifts a block of mass 10 kg which is at rest from a horizontal ground vertically upward, to a height of 20 m.

Find:

(a) the time taken to lift the block, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Data note: the question gives neither the speed nor the acceleration of the block. The only reading that allows a time to be found from the data is the one the numbers are built for: the block starts from rest and moves through $20$ m with acceleration $g=10\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.*

Use $s=ut+\frac12at^2$ with $u=0$, $s=20$, $a=10$:

$$20=\frac12(10)t^2=5t^2\ \Longrightarrow\ t^2=4\ \Longrightarrow\ t=2.$$

**The time taken is $2$ s.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the work done against gravity by the crane, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Work done against gravity = weight $\times$ height lifted $=mgh$:

$$W=10\times10\times20=2\,000.$$

**The work done against gravity is $2\,000$ J.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the power generated by the crane. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Power $=\dfrac{\text{work done}}{\text{time taken}}=\dfrac{2\,000}{2}=1\,000$.

**The (average) power generated by the crane is $1\,000$ W.** (It uses the time $2$ s found in (a).)
